newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan property talks at stalemate.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan property talks at stalemate.

text.p: Representatives of Nicaragua's government and the left-wing Sandinista opposition met late on Thursday to negotiate a solution to Nicaragua's property problem amid hardened positions on both sides.

It was the parties' second meeting to resolve the legal conflicts left from the 1979-1990 Sandinista government, when the state confiscated thousands of private properties creating disputes between the former and current occupants.
The first meeting between the bitter rivals, which took place Jan. 27, was heralded as a major step toward political stability in Nicaragua.
But Thursday's talks showed a quick solution was not going to be easy as both sides hardened their positions, agreeing to meet again on Feb. 13 to continue the negotiations.

Vice President Enrique Bolanos, the head of the government delegation, told a news conference the government demanded that the Sandinista Front return all the confiscated property in its hands, a demand rejected by the Sandinista delegation putting the parties in seemingly irreconcilable positions.
Bayardo Arce, heading the Sandinista delegation, told reporters the confiscations were legal. "All the confiscated properties were products of the robbery of the (former dictator Anastasio) Somoza."
Somoza was toppled in the 1979 Sandinista revolution and his properties confiscated.
Bolanos said the government would take legal steps if the Sandinistas refused to return the properties.
Bolanos also announced the government would start returning the confiscated properties in the hands of the state to their original owners.

In a flurry of legislation before leaving office after their 1990 election loss to former President Violeta Chamorro, the Sandinistas awarded themselves more than 200,000 properties they had confiscated.
